reports.name: Strategy
reports.email_summary: Strategy resumes BTC buying with cash (not new shares) after 3-week pause; stock jumps ~8-16%.
reports.bottom_line: Strategy funded its return to Bitcoin accumulation entirely from existing USD Cash rather than dilutive ATM issuance, a mild positive for BTC-per-share math, while continuing to retire STRC preferred toward par. The moves, paired with a supportive week for BTC price, drove a sharp share-price recovery, though mNAV remains near parity (~1.04x), limiting the accretive power of any future equity-funded purchases.
source_conflicts: mNAV estimates vary by source and date: mnav.com shows a live 1.04x, bitcointreasuries.net showed 1.06x (EV) / 0.78-0.79x (basic/diluted) as of Aug 31, and other trackers cited 0.68x basic as of Aug 3 — figures are not directly comparable due to differing dates and methodologies (EV vs basic vs diluted).

updates.headline: Strategy resumes BTC buys, 950 BTC funded by cash
updates.what_happened: Strategy filed an 8-K disclosing it purchased 950 BTC for $75.7 million (avg $79,670/BTC) during September 14-20, ending a roughly three-week pause. Critically, the purchase was funded entirely from existing USD Cash rather than new share or ATM issuance, and total holdings rose to 846,000 BTC at an average cost of $75,416.
updates.thesis_fit: Accumulation funded from cash rather than new equity increases BTC per diluted share without adding dilution, directly supporting the core treasury-flywheel thesis.

updates.headline: STRC preferred buyback grows to $174M for the week
updates.what_happened: The same 8-K disclosed Strategy repurchased 1,771,238 shares of STRC preferred for $174.0 million during September 14-20, up from $139.3 million the prior week, funded from USD Cash. As of September 20, USD Reserve stood at $5.04 billion and USD Cash at $1.05 billion, after also using $57.4 million of the USD Reserve for preferred dividends and debt interest.
updates.thesis_fit: Continued STRC buybacks push the preferred back toward par and stabilize the digital-credit stack, but draw down cash that could otherwise fund additional BTC purchases.

updates.headline: MSTR stock surges over 8% on BTC purchase news
updates.what_happened: MSTR shares rose more than 8% in premarket trading Monday, extending a prior week's 17% weekly gain, after the company disclosed the resumed bitcoin buying and preferred repurchase. The move pushed the stock back into positive territory for the year, following weeks of pressure tied to forced BTC/stock sales to meet preferred dividend obligations.
updates.thesis_fit: Share price reaction reflects renewed confidence in the accumulation flywheel, though the stock remains a high-beta BTC proxy far below its 52-week high.

reports.name: Metaplanet

snapshot.holdings: 43,000 BTC (last confirmed purchase disclosed July 2, 2026; no new purchase confirmed in the last 3 days)

reports.email_summary: VanEck's mid-September ChainCheck rates Metaplanet the only 'Bad' governance grade among top-10 Bitcoin treasuries, reiterating dilution concerns.
reports.bottom_line: No new BTC purchases, financing, or shareholder-change filings emerged in the last three days; the sole development is a VanEck research note doubling down on prior dilution/governance criticism and arguing the September 11 pool cut is insufficient. This keeps governance risk in the spotlight without materially changing BTC-per-share economics.
source_conflicts: mNAV figures are stale and inconsistent across trackers as of Sept 21: mnav.com shows 1.21x based on a ~40,177 BTC snapshot roughly a month old, while other June 2026 sources cite readings near 0.90x-0.92x; no reliable same-day figure was found, so mNAV is reported as null.

BTC treasury ranking is inconsistent across sources: some (VanEck-linked and July 2026 press) still call Metaplanet the 3rd-largest corporate holder at 43,000 BTC, while CoinGecko's treasury tracker lists it as 6th-largest with 43,000 BTC worth $3.65B — likely reflecting differing peer-set cutoff dates rather than a change in Metaplanet's own holdings.

updates.headline: VanEck rates Metaplanet 'Bad' on executive pay, dilution
updates.what_happened: VanEck's mid-September 2026 Bitcoin ChainCheck report singled out Metaplanet as the only company among the ten largest digital-asset treasuries it grades 'Bad' on executive compensation practices, saying its option pool equals roughly 14.7% of fully diluted shares and officer exposure is about 8.2% — far above peer averages. The report acknowledges the board's August 18 removal of the automatic pool-growth clause and the September 11 cut of the option pool by 41% to 188.2 million shares, but argues these fixes still fall short and calls for a full reversal of the roughly 273 million shares added via the prior mechanism plus a shareholder-approved replacement plan.
updates.thesis_fit: This is a direct governance/incentive-alignment critique from a reputable crypto-focused asset manager, reinforcing the checklist concern that compensation structures may not be genuinely performance-linked despite the already-reported 41% pool cut.

reports.name: Asset Entities / Strive

snapshot.holdings: 26,355 BTC as of September 18, 2026 (up from 25,000 BTC reported the prior week)

reports.email_summary: Strive bought another 1,355 BTC ($107.7M) to reach 26,355 BTC, funded partly by newly-active warrant exercises alongside SATA preferred sales.
reports.bottom_line: Strive continued its weekly accumulation cadence, adding 1,355 BTC and diversifying financing with $21.2M of warrant-exercise proceeds alongside SATA preferred sales, which modestly eases reliance on dilutive preferred issuance. Continued share-count growth and an elevated market premium to Bitcoin NAV keep dilution and valuation-support risk as the key swing factors for the thesis.
source_conflicts: mNAV/premium figures vary by source and date: mnav.com cites 1.67x (as of ~21,356 BTC, three weeks old), an M1 summary cites 1.69x, and Yahoo Finance references a '90% NAV premium' tied to the 25,000 BTC disclosure — no single up-to-date mNAV figure could be confirmed for the 26,355 BTC holding as of Sept 18-21.

updates.headline: Strive buys 1,355 BTC for $107.7M, holdings hit 26,355
updates.what_happened: Strive disclosed via 8-K that it purchased 1,355 bitcoin between September 14 and September 18, 2026 at an average price of about $79,475 per coin, inclusive of fees, taking total holdings to 26,355 BTC. Class A common shares outstanding rose by 2,073,760 to 87,804,613 and cash grew to $229.6 million, a $25.4 million increase from September 11, while SATA preferred shares outstanding rose by 786,194 to 11,184,160.
updates.thesis_fit: Continues the core Bitcoin-accumulation narrative that underpins the treasury-wrapper thesis, but the accompanying rise in Class A shares outstanding is an ongoing dilution data point to track against Bitcoin-per-share growth.

updates.headline: Warrant exercises begin, add $21.2M, diversify funding mix
updates.what_happened: CEO Matt Cole disclosed that warrant exercises began during the week and generated $21.2 million in gross proceeds, with SATA preferred sales supplying the remainder of capital for the latest BTC purchase. Including the warrant proceeds, SATA accounted for 57.7% of total capital raised for the week, a lower share than in prior all-preferred weeks.
updates.thesis_fit: Warrant exercises give Strive a second capital-raising lever beyond the daily-paying 13% SATA preferred, which can reduce dependence on high-cost preferred dividends versus existing shareholders over time.

reports.name: BitMine Immersion

snapshot.holdings: 5,983,940 ETH (~4.9% of ETH supply); 5,067,309 ETH staked (85% of holdings); 212 BTC; $180M Beast Industries stake; $105M Eightco (ORBS) stake; $714M cash & marketable securities; total crypto+cash+moonshots $17.1B

reports.email_summary: BitMine's Sept 21 weekly 8-K shows ETH holdings and staking revenue projections both rising as it nears its 5% supply target.
reports.bottom_line: The latest primary-source treasury update shows continued disciplined weekly ETH accumulation and rising projected staking revenue, reinforcing the core accumulation thesis. No new financing, dilution, or governance red flags surfaced in the window, though the company remains a high-risk, loss-making vehicle whose value is entirely tied to ETH price and execution.
source_conflicts: Share price snapshots conflict across sources in the window: CNN/bmnr.rocks show a close of $25.99-$27.26 (+8.79%) while Robinhood shows $25.85 as of Sept 19 and other trackers show $20.98-$22.47 on different dates; these appear to reflect different intraday/closing snapshots rather than a single conflicting figure.

ETH holdings value is quoted variably at $16.1B-$16.3B for the same 5,983,940 ETH figure depending on the ETH spot price used (~$2,688 per Coinbase vs. other timestamps), which is a pricing-timestamp difference rather than a substantive holdings discrepancy.

updates.headline: BitMine's weekly 8-K: ETH holdings hit 5.98M, 98% to 5% goal
updates.what_happened: In a Form 8-K filed September 21, 2026, BitMine disclosed it bought 27,562 ETH over the prior week, lifting total holdings to 5,983,940 ETH (4.9% of the 122.1M ETH supply) and total crypto/cash/moonshot holdings to $17.1 billion. The company said it is now 98% of the way to Tom Lee's 'Alchemy of 5%' target after 15 months, and staked ETH remained at 5,067,309 tokens (85% of holdings), with annualized staking revenue projections rising to $357 million from $334 million the prior week, and a theoretical fully-staked run rate of $421 million.
updates.thesis_fit: Continued weekly ETH accumulation funded without new dilutive share issuance disclosed this week, plus rising staking-yield economics, directly supports the credible-accumulation and staking-economics pillars of the thesis.

updates.headline: Tom Lee to keynote Korea Blockchain Week Sept 30
updates.what_happened: The same Sept 21 press release confirmed Chairman Tom Lee will deliver a keynote at Korea Blockchain Week on September 30, 2026, in Seoul, reiterating his view that a new crypto bull market began in late June 2026 and that ETH has outperformed the S&P 500 by 6,519 basis points quarter-to-date.
updates.thesis_fit: A high-visibility public appearance reinforces the narrative/marketing side of the thesis but is not itself a treasury, financing, or governance action.

sector.bottom_line: With the CLARITY Act stalled in the Senate, U.S. regulators (CFTC, SEC, OCC) are advancing crypto market-structure and capital-markets access piecemeal via existing authority, expanding derivatives products and stablecoin bank charters rather than waiting for comprehensive legislation.

updates.headline: CFTC broadens no-action relief for crypto wallet software
updates.what_happened: The CFTC's Market Participants Division issued Staff Letter 26-25, expanding a no-action position previously limited to Phantom Technologies to cover any qualifying 'passive software' provider (wallets, DeFi front ends, apps) that routes users to CFTC-registered derivatives venues without requiring introducing-broker registration. The relief lasts until the Commission finalizes formal rulemaking and does not shield providers from other laws such as money-transmission or DOJ criminal statutes.

updates.headline: Coinbase, Kalshi, Bitnomial file for single-stock perpetual futures
updates.what_happened: Coinbase Derivatives, Kalshi, and Kraken-linked Bitnomial each filed proposed rule changes with the SEC/CFTC on September 18 to list cash-settled, no-expiry perpetual futures on individual U.S. stocks and ETFs (Apple, Tesla, Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon, SPY, QQQ among proposed underliers). CFTC approval remains pending for all three filings, and the products would give price exposure only, without ownership, dividend, or voting rights.

updates.headline: Bastion wins conditional OCC national trust bank charter
updates.what_happened: Stablecoin infrastructure provider Bastion received preliminary conditional OCC approval to convert its New York trust charter into a national trust bank charter (Bastion Platforms National Trust Company), covering GENIUS Act-compliant stablecoin custody, wallets, payment infrastructure, and white-label issuance. The charter bars deposit-taking and lending and is not FDIC-insured, joining Ripple, Circle, and BitGo among firms securing similar federal stablecoin charters.
